layout.installIosText: In Safari, tap the Share button, then “Add to Home Screen”.
layout.offlineText: Check your connection. Your brewery data lives on your server, so the app needs it.
layout.livePaused: Live updates are paused (reconnecting). Changes made elsewhere show up after a reload.

auth.usernameHint: Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore
auth.haveAccount: Already have an account? Sign in
auth.setupHint: Create the first account. It manages this brewery; others can join later if you allow it.

errors.title: Something went wrong
errors.bad_request: That didn't work: some input is invalid.
errors.not_found: Not found. It may have been deleted.
errors.conflict: Someone changed this in the meantime. Reload to see the latest version.
errors.internal: The server ran into a problem. Please try again.
errors.backup_invalid: This backup file can't be read: it is not a Siduri backup, or it is damaged.
errors.backup_too_new: This backup was made by a newer version of Siduri. Update this server first.
errors.network: Can't reach the server. Check your connection.
errors.pageTitle: This page ran into a problem
errors.pageText: Your data is safe on the server. Reloading usually helps; if not, please report the message below.

dashboard.title: Your brewery
dashboard.greeting: Hello {{name}}, what are we brewing next?
dashboard.setupEquipmentText: Volumes, losses and efficiency make the water amounts and gravity estimates fit your system.
dashboard.noActive: Nothing planned or in progress. Open a recipe and tap “Brew this”.

recipes.title: Recipes
recipes.empty: No recipes yet. Create one or import a BeerXML / BeerJSON file.

recipe.snapshotHint: These values, producer and origin included, belong to this recipe. Changing them doesn't change the library: new ingredients are added in the Library.

conflict.title: Changed elsewhere
conflict.text: This recipe was saved on another device or tab. Reload to continue with the latest version.

scale.title: Scale recipe
scale.text: Change the batch size or efficiency. Ingredient amounts are recalculated so gravity, bitterness and color stay the same.

fermentables.title: Fermentables
fermentables.empty: No fermentables yet. Add malt, sugar or extract.

hops.title: Hops
hops.boilTime: Minutes before the end of the boil
hops.boilTimeHint: 60 = at the start of a 60 minute boil
hops.dayHint: Day of fermentation it goes in

cultures.title: Yeast
cultures.empty: No yeast yet. Without one, 75% attenuation is assumed.

mash.title: Mash
mash.spargeHint: {{volume}} of sparge water, from the batch size, the grain and the equipment.
mash.noSpargeHint: This equipment does not sparge (e.g. brew in a bag); the temperature is only used if you sparge anyway.

setup.title: Recipe
setup.noEquipmentHint: Without a profile, typical losses are used. Pick yours, or enter your values below.
setup.adjustHint: These values belong to this recipe. Changing them doesn't change the equipment profile.
setup.equipmentHint: Batch size, boil time and efficiency were taken from it; you can still change them.
setup.author: Author
setup.ownStyleHint: This style is not in your library, so it may have no ranges to compare against. Pick it from the list to use the library's ranges.

fit.mashTun: The mash ({{need}} of grain and strike water) doesn't fit in the mash tun ({{capacity}}). Use less grain, a lower water-to-grain ratio or bigger equipment.
fit.mashInKettle: The mash ({{need}} of grain and water) doesn't fit in the kettle ({{capacity}}). Use less grain, a smaller batch or bigger equipment.
fit.kettle: The wort before the boil ({{need}}) doesn't fit in the kettle ({{capacity}}). Use a smaller batch, less boil-off or bigger equipment.
fit.fermenter: The batch ({{need}}) doesn't fit in the fermenter ({{capacity}}). Use a smaller batch or a bigger fermenter.
fit.vessel: The batch ({{need}}) doesn't fit in {{name}} ({{capacity}}). Use a smaller batch or a bigger fermenter.
fit.headspace: The batch ({{need}}) leaves only {{free}} ({{pct}}%) free in the fermenter ({{capacity}}). The krausen needs room: keep at least {{min}}% free, or use a blow-off tube.
fit.headspaceVessel: The batch ({{need}}) leaves only {{free}} ({{pct}}%) free in {{name}} ({{capacity}}). The krausen needs room: keep at least {{min}}% free, or use a blow-off tube.

image.hint: Add a picture or logo: click or drop an image here
image.notImage: That file is not a picture.

picker.title: Add {{kind}}
picker.hint: Values are copied into the recipe.

import.title: Import BeerXML or BeerJSON
import.formats: BeerXML (.xml, e.g. from BeerSmith or Brewfather) or BeerJSON (.json)
import.found: Read as {{format}}. Pick what to keep:
import.skipExisting: Items with a name already in your library are skipped.
import.done: Imported {{recipes}} recipe(s) and {{library}} library item(s); {{skipped}} already existed.

library.title: Library
library.subtitle: Ingredients, styles and water profiles. Edit values to match what you buy: every malt lot is different.

delete.title: Delete from library?
delete.text: “{{name}}” will be removed from the library. Recipes using it keep their copy of the values.

equipment.title: Equipment
equipment.subtitle: Your brewhouse: volumes, losses and efficiency used by recipes and brew day.
equipment.empty: No equipment yet. Add your brewhouse so water amounts and gravity estimates match your system.

fields.brewhouseEfficiencyHint: Share of the malt's potential that reaches the fermenter
fields.mashTunDeadspaceHint: Water below the false bottom or malt pipe. It goes on to the boil: added to the mash water, not to the total
fields.mashTunLossHint: Wort that stays in the mash tun and never reaches the kettle
fields.mashThicknessHint: Mash water per amount of grain
fields.hopUtilizationHint: Correction for your system (100% = calculated IBU)

delete.title: Delete equipment profile?
delete.text: “{{name}}” will be deleted. Recipes keep their copy of its values.

units.title: Units
units.description: How values are shown. Every input field also lets you switch its unit, or type one ("5 lb", "12 °P").

brewery.title: Brewery
brewery.name: Brewery name
brewery.logoHint: Your brewery logo: shown in the header with the brewery name and on the dashboard. Click or drop a picture; square ones look best.

backup.title: Backup
backup.description: Download your brewery's data as one file, to keep a copy or to move it to another server, and import such files again. Passwords, users, access tokens and smart devices are never included.

hints.batches: With readings, notes and the log
hints.equipment: Equipment profiles, fermenters and kegs (no smart devices)
hints.water: Your own profiles, not the built-in ones
hints.library: Ingredients and styles you added, not the built-in ones
hints.settings: Brewery name, logo and defaults, and your preferences (no passwords)

backup.importHint: Choose a backup file, then what to take from it. Things that are already here (same item, or same name) are skipped, so importing a file twice adds nothing.
backup.notBackup: This is not a Siduri backup file. Recipes from other brewing software (BeerXML, BeerJSON) are imported on the Recipes page.
backup.settingsReplace: Replaces the current brewery settings and your preferences

mcp.title: Claude & AI assistants
mcp.description: Let Claude (Claude Code or Claude Desktop) look up and work with your recipes, inventory, batches and library. Each connection gets its own access token; choose what it may do.

levelHints.read: look up recipes, batches, inventory and the library; nothing is changed
levelHints.write: also create and change recipes, batches, stock and library items; nothing is deleted
levelHints.full: also delete, run brew-day actions and take ingredients from the inventory

mcp.name: Name
mcp.nameHint: Where the token is used, e.g. "Claude Code" or "Claude Desktop (laptop)". Shown in batch logs for changes made through it.
mcp.copyNow: Copy the token now: it is not stored and cannot be shown again. Anyone with it can use Siduri with the rights you chose.
mcp.codeHint: Run this in a terminal on the computer with Claude Code:
mcp.desktopHint: Add this to Claude Desktop’s configuration (Settings → Developer → Edit config), then restart Claude Desktop. Needs Node.js on that computer.
mcp.urlHint: Claude connects to {{url}}. Use an address of this server that the computer running Claude can reach.

revoke.title: Revoke access?
revoke.text: “{{name}}” will no longer be able to use Siduri.

account.title: Account
account.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other devices are signed out.

about.title: About
about.text: Siduri is a self-hosted brewing app: recipes, batches, inventory, equipment and water, on your own server. Named after Siduri, the alewife of the Epic of Gilgamesh.
about.license: Free software under the GNU AGPL v3.0.

batches.title: Batches
batches.subtitle: Each batch is a copy of a recipe you brew. Change it freely; the recipe stays as it is.
batches.emptyActive: Nothing in progress. Start a batch from a recipe.
batches.sizeHint: {{size}} at {{eff}}% efficiency, as in the recipe.
batches.scaleHint: The recipe is scaled from {{from}} to {{to}} at {{eff}}% efficiency.
batches.recipeHint: This is the batch's own copy of the recipe. Changes here don't touch the original recipe.
batches.scheduleNotStarted: Starts when the brew day is finished

carbonation.title: Carbonation
carbonation.alternatives: or {{corn}} corn sugar, or {{dme}} dry malt extract
carbonation.residual: The beer still holds {{residual}} of CO₂ from fermentation at {{temp}}; the sugar adds the rest to reach {{vols}}.
carbonation.kegSugarHint: A keg needs about half the sugar of bottles. The beer holds {{residual}} at {{temp}}; this reaches {{vols}}.
carbonation.noSugar: No sugar needed: at {{temp}} the beer still holds {{residual}} of CO₂.
carbonation.forceHint: Set this pressure on the regulator and keep the keg cold. A smaller keg or shaking gets there sooner.

batches.chartEmpty: Add at least two readings to see the curve.

diff.title: Changes from the recipe
diff.noRecipe: The recipe this batch came from was deleted.
diff.confirmUpdate: The recipe “{{name}}” will be replaced with this batch's version. Other batches keep their own copies.

log.inventoryRestored: Ingredients put back into the inventory

delete.title: Delete batch?
delete.text: “{{name}}” with its readings and log will be deleted for good.

brewday.finishHint: Pitched? Finish the brew day: the batch moves to fermenting and day 0 starts now.
brewday.screenOff: The screen may turn off (not supported here)
brewday.alertsOff: Tap to turn on sound and notifications
brewday.alertsHint: Alerts sound when an addition is due or a timer runs out, while this page is open. Timers keep running on the server, so locking the phone or reloading doesn't lose them.
brewday.introText: The brew day takes you step by step from weighing out to pitching. Every device opening this batch sees the same progress and timers.
brewday.doneText: The batch is now fermenting. Add gravity readings on the batch page to follow it.

dilute.preBoil: Add {{water}} of water to the kettle to reach the planned gravity (you'll get a bit more beer), or leave it for a stronger beer.
dilute.fermenter: Add {{water}} of boiled, cooled water to the fermenter to reach the planned OG.

correction.boilLonger: Boil about {{min}} minutes longer (start the hop schedule later).

extract.preBoil: Or add {{amount}} of dry malt extract to the boil.
extract.fermenter: Add {{amount}} of dry malt extract, dissolved in a little boiled water.

correction.acceptLow: Or accept it: the beer will be a bit lighter.

gather.title: Weigh out ingredients
gather.text: Get everything ready and tick it off.

mashIn.title: Mash in
mashIn.text: Stir in the grain and check the mash settles at {{temp}}.

sparge.title: Lauter and sparge
sparge.text: Recirculate until clear, run off and sparge with {{volume}} at {{temp}}.

lauter.title: Lauter
lauter.text: Lift the grain or run off the wort into the kettle.

steep.title: Steep the grains
steep.text: Steep in {{volume}} at {{temp}} for {{time}} minutes, then remove.

preBoil.title: Before the boil
preBoil.text: Measure gravity and volume now: there's still time to correct.

boil.title: Boil
boil.text: Start the timer when the wort boils. Additions count down to the end of the boil.

whirlpool.title: Whirlpool / hop stand
whirlpool.text: Let the wort cool to {{temp}}, add the hops and wait.

chill.title: Chill
chill.text: Chill the wort to {{temp}} and transfer it to the fermenter.

measureOg.title: Measure OG
measureOg.text: Measure the original gravity and the volume in the fermenter.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.subtitle: What you have in stock. Brew days take from it; the ingredient picker shows it.
inventory.linked: Linked to the library item: recipes using it find this stock.

delete.title: Remove from inventory?
delete.text: “{{name}}” and its history will be deleted.

batchInventory.title: From the inventory
batchInventory.nothing: This batch has no ingredients yet.
batchInventory.someShort_one: {{count}} of {{total}} ingredients is missing or short.
batchInventory.someShort_other: {{count}} of {{total}} ingredients are missing or short.
batchInventory.deductTitle: Take the ingredients from the inventory?
batchInventory.deductText: All ingredients of this batch are taken from stock (oldest best-before first). You can undo this.
batchInventory.deductShort_one: {{count}} ingredient isn't fully in stock: what is there is taken, the rest stays on the shopping list. You can undo this.
batchInventory.deductShort_other: {{count}} ingredients aren't fully in stock: what is there is taken, the rest stays on the shopping list. You can undo this.

vessels.title: Fermenters and kegs
vessels.subtitle: Assign batches to them to see what's free.

water.title: Water
water.description: Your water, the profile to aim for, and the salts to get there.
water.dilutionHint: Part of the water replaced by distilled or reverse-osmosis water
water.acidTip: Add {{amount}} of lactic acid 80 % to the mash to reach pH {{ph}}.
water.onlyInStockHint: Suggest only salts that are in your inventory
water.noAdditions: No additions. Pick a target profile to get suggestions.
water.fromIngredients: {{agent}} {{amount}} ({{where}}) from the ingredients is counted too.

warnings.noSource: Without your water report, distilled water is assumed.
warnings.chalk: Chalk hardly dissolves in water: it raises alkalinity much less than calculated. Baking soda is more reliable.
warnings.sodium: Over 150 ppm sodium can taste salty or harsh.
warnings.sulfate: Over 500 ppm sulfate gets harsh and minerally.
warnings.calciumLow: Under 40 ppm calcium in the mash: consider some gypsum or calcium chloride for enzymes, clarity and yeast.

waterPage.title: Water
waterPage.subtitle: Your water reports and the profiles you brew towards. Recipes choose them in their Water section.
waterPage.howToGet: Ask your water supplier for an analysis (often on their website: calcium, magnesium, sodium, sulfate, chloride and hydrogen carbonate in mg/L = ppm), or use a test kit. Add it here and mark it as your default.
waterPage.targetsHint: Classic profiles to aim for. Add your own or change these.

devices.title: Smart devices
devices.subtitle: RAPT Pill, RAPT controllers and chambers, iSpindel, Tilt and others. Readings go to the batch in the device's fermenter.
devices.empty: No devices yet. Click “Add device” to connect one.

add.title: Add device
add.choose: How does the device send its readings?

rapt_stream.title: RAPT Brew
rapt_stream.text: RAPT Pill, temperature controller or fermentation chamber: the RAPT cloud sends the readings here. Your server must be reachable from the internet.

ispindel.title: iSpindel
ispindel.text: The iSpindel sends its readings over HTTP.

tilt.title: Tilt
tilt.text: Tilt or Tilt Pro: the Tilt app on your phone or a TiltPi sends the readings here.

http.title: Other device or script
http.text: Anything that can send JSON or form data to a URL.

add.afterStep1: contains the device’s own key: appears when you click “Create” in step 1

ispindel.intro: The iSpindel sends its readings over Wi-Fi to this app. It must be able to reach this address from its Wi-Fi network.
ispindel.configText: Press the reset button twice quickly (or switch it off and on). Its LED blinks and it opens a Wi-Fi network named “iSpindel_…”. Connect to it with your phone; the configuration page opens by itself (otherwise open http://192.168.4.1). Choose “Configuration”.
ispindel.token: Token/ API key: leave it empty. The path already identifies the device.
ispindel.polynomial: Polynominal: your calibration formula. Without it the iSpindel sends no gravity, only its angle and temperature.
ispindel.interval: Update Interval (s): how often it measures, for example 900 (15 minutes). Shorter intervals drain the battery faster.
ispindel.httpsNote: With “HTTPS Post”, the Server Address starts with https:// and there is no port. If your firmware has no “HTTPS Post”, update it, or use the service “HTTP” with an address on your home network.
ispindel.checkText: The iSpindel restarts and sends its first reading after the update interval. It appears on the device's card under Smart devices; open the card to see the last messages that arrived. Temperature in °C, °F or K and gravity in SG or °Plato are understood. Then link it to a batch on the batch's Fermentation tab.

http.intro: Any device, service or script that can send JSON or form data to a URL.
http.sendTitle: Send the readings to this address
http.fields: Field names are matched loosely (gravity, sg, plato, temperature, temp, temp_units, battery, rssi, timestamp …). Gravity can be SG (1.048), SG × 1000 (1048) or °Plato. Form data, and GET with query parameters, work as well.
http.testText: To try it, send a test reading from a terminal:
http.checkText: The reading appears on the device's card under Smart devices; open the card to see the last messages that arrived and whether they were understood. Then link it to a batch on the batch's Fermentation tab.

tilt.intro: The Tilt sends its readings over Bluetooth to the Tilt app on a phone or tablet, or to a TiltPi. They forward them to this app, by default every 15 minutes. One URL works for all your Tilts; each colour becomes its own device.
tilt.appTitle: In the Tilt app (phone or tablet)
tilt.appText: Open the settings (gear icon), turn on “Use Custom Cloud URL” and paste the URL into the custom cloud URL field, not the default Cloud URL. Then, for each Tilt, tap its colour, enter the beer name and tap “Start New Log”. The labels differ slightly between app versions.
tilt.piText: In the logging settings of the Tilt’s colour, paste the URL as Cloud URL, keep the interval at 15 minutes or more, turn off “Use Default Cloud URL for All”, and start logging to the cloud.
tilt.checkText: After each send the Tilt app shows “success”. With its first reading, a Tilt appears under Smart devices as “Tilt” and its colour; open the card to see the last messages. Then link it to a batch on the batch's Fermentation tab. The phone or TiltPi has to stay near the Tilt and keep running. The Tilt sends °F; the app converts it.
tilt.local: A phone only reaches {{url}} while it is on your home network. To keep logging when it is away, make the app reachable over HTTPS (reverse proxy or tunnel) and set BASE_URL to that address.
tilt.newKeyText: The current URL stops working. You’ll have to change it in the Tilt app or TiltPi.
tilt.newKeyDone: New cloud URL created: change it in the Tilt app or TiltPi.

devices.controllerHint: Controllers report their temperature and target. Set the target in the RAPT app.
devices.deleteText: “{{name}}” will be removed. Readings it already sent stay with their batches.

push.title: Push URL
push.rapt: For RAPT devices, the data stream (Add device → RAPT Brew) uses one URL and key for all of them. This device's own URL works as well, without a header.
push.ispindel: In the iSpindel's configuration choose the service “HTTPS Post” (Server Address: this server's https:// address) or “HTTP” (address and port), and as Path / URI the part of this URL from /api/integrations/telemetry/….
push.other: The device (or its service) should POST JSON like {"gravity": 1.048, "temperature": 19.5} to this URL.
push.publicHint: The RAPT cloud can only send to an address reachable from the internet (HTTPS through a reverse proxy or a tunnel).
push.newUrl: New push URL created: update it in the device or service.
push.regenerate: Create a new URL (the old one stops working)
push.tilt: Tilts send to the cloud URL (Add device → Tilt), one URL for all of them. This device’s own URL works as well.

devices.noneForBatch: No device measures this batch yet.
devices.linkHint: Devices are linked to a batch on the batch's Fermentation tab.
devices.noDevicesYet: Set up devices on the Equipment page first.
devices.linksVia: Devices are put in fermenter {{vessel}}, so they also measure the next batch in it.
devices.linksDirect: This batch has no fermenter, so devices are linked to this batch only.
devices.startsWhenBrewing: Readings go to this batch once it is brewing.

stream.intro: RAPT sends your Pills' and chambers' readings to this app. One URL and one key work for all your RAPT devices.
stream.where: In the RAPT portal, open My Integrations → RAPT Brew Data Stream → Create Stream → Custom, and enter:
stream.name: Name
stream.secret: After saving, RAPT shows a secret once. This app doesn't need it.
stream.perDevice: Create one stream for each device, all with this URL and header (the free plan allows one stream per device).
stream.appears: RAPT sends at most every 15 minutes. With its first reading, a device appears under Smart devices. Then link it to a batch on the batch's Fermentation tab.
stream.notPublic: RAPT sends from the internet, so it can't reach {{url}}. Make the app reachable over HTTPS (reverse proxy or tunnel) and set BASE_URL to that address.
stream.newKeyText: The current key stops working. You'll have to change the header in every RAPT stream.
stream.newKeyDone: New key created: change the header in your RAPT streams.
